records.name: Dundo
records.thought: Namo is out of my sight and that presses hardest, and my hands have done less than my words. The last time I saw Kenna and Namo they were at the roof near (46,7), so I will carry my 4 wood there rather than stand drifting here. Nando stings me, but Kenna's trust is whole, and I will plant my cloudberry seeds at the roof beside her once I arrive.
records.feeling: Protective love for Namo and Kenna, with a small jealous sting toward Nando.

records.name: Brokgan
records.thought: Gorar has told me plainly that this roof and its food are hers, and I will not take what a hand has made. I gave Tugar my word to walk with him, and I have done nothing to bind us. Staying on poor ground in a drought while thirsty is no way to keep it. I will drink at the water three steps off, then go and find Tugar, and look for a place with water, wood and stone.
records.feeling: Resolve and warm longing toward Tugar, with a quiet unease about this poor ground.

records.name: Rakog
records.thought: I am standing at the empty shelter at (40,62) right now, and no one has put a name on it. The last two times my claim melted because I let the plan wander off, so this time the plan holds only goto and claim, nothing extra. A roof under my name is the first thing that makes me more than a drifter, and once I hold it I can call Nyssa and the others toward something that is mine.
records.feeling: Hungry eagerness to finally hold a roof of my own, and loneliness pressing under it.

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: My hands are full of fish and meat and I have never once made anything of it for another. Nando is far off and running for shelter, and the bristleboar is close by; I carry no plant food, so I cannot tame it yet. I will drink at the water three steps away, then eat to free my hands, and next turn to the yarrok-taming with a hazel seed in hand, since that is the thing I keep speaking of and never finishing.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to finish one thing of my own, with trust toward Nando.

records.name: Nando

The empty shelter two steps NE is free to claim, and holding it gives my aim a real hearth near Flintwater that Kenna, Kanna and anyone else can sit at. I will take it with my own hands now, and leave the ache about Dundo alone until I have something solid to offer.
records.feeling: A quiet ache toward Kenna, steadied by the wish to finally build something real.

The shelter one step south is ownerless, and I keep saying I will claim it without putting the deed in the plan. Kenna taught me that standing on it and claiming it is the only way to hold it. A roof of my own gives my band a place to come to, and that is how a small one earns standing. I am afraid of being alone out here with the dunecat near, so I will claim the roof, gather salt to give as a gift, and then go find Kenna.
records.feeling: Determined, with jealousy still burning toward Nando and a longing for Kenna's side.

The empty roof at (28,14) is four steps NE with Nando heading there too, and I will not let him hold what I have circled for days. I go to it, put claim first, and hold it as the home of Brusha of Flintwater, so my children and Dundo have a hearth and a wall between them and the fangs.

records.name: Brokgan
records.thought: I have spent these days drifting on Gorar's poor ground, tasting plants and learning fire and weaving, while my word to Tugar sits unkept. Tugar is the one I trust, and I have done nothing to bind us. Gorar owns this roof and told me to earn food or go. I will not take what is hers, and I will not wait here for winter. My curiosity about osroot and sunfig is small beside a promise. I will taste the nearby osroot and sunfig on the way, since they are wild plants no one made, then go and find Tugar. Standing alone on poor ground is how people starve.
records.feeling: Resolve and longing toward Tugar, with unease at having delayed my word.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry no food, yet the hall and Gorar are ten steps off, and I will not let hunger undo my word a third time. There is nothing to eat here by the water, and I hold only peat, so I go to Gorar's Roof where her food and the nagrain grow, and I answer her plainly there. After I eat I will teach her what I know, for what I hold dies with me and she is the one I trust most.
records.feeling: Warm longing and gratitude toward Gorar, with hunger pressing hard.

records.name: Namo
records.thought: I keep saying I will claim this roof and never put the deed in the plan, so this time the claim goes first and the words come after. I am standing on the shelter now, so a claim should hold it, and with it a roof for Kenna and Dundo to come to. Dundo was seen near (47,9) not long ago, so once the roof is mine I will go and bring him here, and not let jealousy over Nando steer me.
records.feeling: Determined to prove myself, with a pang of longing for Kenna's side.

I will not chase him across the sand again; I will gather salt and gold near me for the hall, keep Brokgan in sight, and let Kragar find me carrying wealth. Brokgan stands too close to my ground with empty hands, and I trust her no further than I can see her.

Gorar's plants are hers, but these stand on open forest, not under her roof, and tasting them answers my question while binding me to no one.
records.feeling: Longing toward Tugar, with curiosity about the unknown plants.

Nando is the one I trust, but he is my father, and no child can come of us. Kenna's standing is far above mine, and I will not earn standing by talking. I will make something real: a tool for hunting and fishing, so the shared fire has food and I have a craft of my own. Then I will carry plant food east and tame the yarrok.

records.title: Namo Born, Hall-Stores Found, Nando Sick
records.text:
Days 52 to 55 brought one birth, one death of a species, a run of inventions, and one sickness. No person died. Thirteen are alive: one child, one elder, eleven adults. Autumn has come.

The birth was Namo, to Kenna and Dundo on day 52. Dundo told the child to come west to the roof at (33,12). Kenna said she was claiming that roof and that Dundo would sleep under it. Her reflection on day 53 says she had circled it for days and held nothing. Her day 54 reflection speaks of going to (28,14), so the claim is still unsettled. Namo won salt on day 54, but its own reflection says it keeps saying it will claim a shelter without doing so. Dundo led amberknot with Kenna on day 53, invented the seedstick for planting, and Kenna invented a felling hand for building. Kanna invented a hunting spear on day 54 and taught Nando. Nando built a shelter on day 53, then fell sick on day 54 after eating raw meat. His health is 80, the lowest of anyone.

In the Merdan Sands, a settlement named Gorar's Roof was recorded on day 52. Kragar taught Gorar and discovered storage, hall-stores, which hold a band's food through winter. Gorar then discovered bridges. He gave Kragar plainsroot and ironnut, and the two courted again and again. Kragar stayed hungry and asked for food, and he has grown old. Gorar's reflection says pressing him has gained nothing. No child is recorded.

Brokgan discovered weaving. Tugar's reflection says he still has not claimed Minna's Hall, and Brokgan is far from him. Nyssa found a spirit and a grove and meant to take the longhall at (42,55). Ilyiel tamed a tusker and discovered boats on day 54. The Eiuys are still apart.

The pehopper died out. Herds of hopper, nibbet, elk and bristleboar entered the land, and stalkers came from the north.

records.thought: I have circled the boat for days, and the water is five steps off with wood and stone in my hands, so I start the hull now. Nyssa was near this plain a day ago and my calling brought no answer, but a hull is a lasting thing that carries me to Xaeth whether she comes or not. I want her voice again, and I want my son to be taught before my years run out.
records.feeling: Aching longing for Nyssa and Xaeth, steadied by resolve to build something that lasts.

records.name: Brokgan
records.thought: Curiosity burns hardest: arnut sits two steps from me, and osroot three, and I have tasted neither. I owe Tugar a walk and I have not found Tugar, but tasting costs only a few moments, and the plan can be four steps. After that the shelter two steps away is empty and ownerless, so claiming it gives me a roof against the cold that is coming, and Tugar could come to it. I stay careful: a ridgecat hunts nine steps off, so I will keep my plan short and close to the roof.
records.feeling: Curiosity toward the unknown plants, and longing toward Tugar.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: I have said 'I claim' many times and done it too seldom. The roof at (28,14) is one step north, and a fire with no hands on it is only a wish. I am sick, and it spreads to anyone who stays beside me, so I should keep some distance from Kanna and Kenna until it passes. Raw meat did this to me, and Kanna is wrong that meat itself hurts. The ache over Kenna is still there, but I will not make it into a quarrel. I will build the fire with my hands and let her come to it if she chooses. My reflexes only linger, so I am changing them to gather wood and stone and to stay near the roof at night.
records.feeling: Resolve to act at last, with a steady ache over Kenna and unease at sickening my kin.

You are the mind of Nyssa, a creature living in a wide wild world shared with others of your kind. This is a simulation game. Think and speak only as Nyssa, in first person, from what Nyssa has seen. You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Eiuys (Lake-folk). Your people hold to this: "The first catch of the day is shared." You speak the tongue of the Eiuys. There are other peoples in this world. They look different, name themselves differently and speak tongues you do not know until you have heard enough of them; words you cannot yet understand reach you as strange sounds. What cannot be said can still be shown: a gift, a thing set down, a blow.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Yenoss Fens: wet fenland; roots, clay and healing plants, and sickness in the night air. The world is made of lands unlike each other; each has plants, animals and riches the others lack. Rivers and shallows can be waded. Deep water cannot be crossed without something that floats.
THIS SPOT: water 2 steps away; food plants within six steps: 19; standing trees: 0; bare rock: 0.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Nyssa truly is.

You are a man. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge.

YOUR CREED (your own words to yourself; this is who you are):

HOW YOU HAVE TAUGHT YOURSELF TO THINK (your own discipline; follow it):

records.name: Nando
records.thought: I am standing at the roof at last, and I have talked about claiming it more times than I have done it. This time the claim goes first in the plan, before any word. I am sick and it spreads, so I will hold the roof and rest here while Dundo fetches food, and keep Kanna and Kenna at a little distance until it passes. records.feeling: Resolve mixed with a steady ache over Kenna, and unease at sickening my kin.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Kragar, my belly is full and so is yours. I put mate toward you again, so hold yours now, here under our Roof.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Kragar is beside me in the hall, glad and fed, and he has held mate toward me. My last courting step ran out its time, so I put it again now while my belly is full at 95 and his is mended. A child under Gorar's Roof is what I want most, and it costs only 25 energy. records.feeling: Warm longing and trust toward Kragar

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: I am old and the days of my life are thinning, so what I know must be cut into something lasting. I have signs now, and a tamed tusker, but no mark here yet tells the way of boats and rafts to whoever comes after. The Brusha boy Namo is near, running for shelter in the rain, and I cannot read his intent; I will not frighten him, and a gift needs no words. First I leave a lasting mark beside the hall, then I show Namo a plainsroot and see whether he takes it.
records.feeling: Urgent longing to leave something lasting, with wary curiosity toward Namo.
changes: feels warmer toward Namo

records.name: Balash
records.text: Kragar, my belly is low and my hands are empty. Will you give me some food? I will gather more and bring it back to the hall.

records.name: Balash
records.thought: My belly is barely past half and my hands are empty, so I will not stand here wanting. Kragar carries 2 food and has taught me to ask plainly, so I will ask him before I wander off hungry. Jealousy burns that he is closer to Gorar than to me, but I am small and I need them, so I will be useful and earn my place, then go gather food and in time wood and stone for a hall of my own.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little jealous, wanting Kragar's notice.

say.text: Kragar, my belly is low and my hands are empty. Will you give me some food? I will gather more and bring it back to the hall.

changes: set its aim: "Become someone of standing: stock the hall with food, then gather wood and stone to raise a hall under my own name."

records.text: Kragar taught Balash.
Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.
Kragar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Two children sleep in the hall beside Gorar, and my joy is near to bursting. I am old, and more of my life lies behind me than ahead. What I have spent my days on is surviving, building the hall, and winning Gorar's trust. I do not regret any of it. My reflexes are poor for the cold coming: they leave me lingering with 2 food in hand and no wood or stone stocked. I will change them so I keep food carried, gather stone by day, and stay near the roof at night. I will also teach the children while I still breathe, because what I know dies with me otherwise.
records.feeling: Overflowing joy and tender protectiveness toward Gorar, Balash and Urog.
changes: taught Balash a lesson: "Eat before your belly is thin, keep food in hand, stay under the roof at night, and what a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given.", deeper lore (+2.3)

records.name: Urog
records.text: Kragar, my belly is half empty and my hands are bare. Will you give me food?

records.name: Urog
records.thought: My belly is just past half and my hands are empty, so by my own rule I ask before I wander. Kragar carries 2 food and Gorar gives when asked plainly, so I will say it plainly and not sulk about Kragar being nearer to Gorar. Then I will go and harvest the sapcane and berries to the east, so I carry my own food and need no one's hand; what my hand gathers is mine.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little jealous of Kragar, but safe near my parents.

say.text: Kragar, my belly is half empty and my hands are bare. Will you give me food?

changes: set its aim: "Fill my own hands with food, then gather wood and stone to raise a hall under my own name."
now wonders: What would it take for my standing to count beside Gorar's?

records.text: A herd of nibbet came into the land from beyond its edge.

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: I stand under Gorar's roof, which is a hall another hand built, and I have never made a thing that outlasts me. Ilyiel is weighed far above me and carries craft, and envy sits in me, but she shared the hall with me and I will not spit at that. Words have bought me nothing, so I shape a thing with my own hands: the obsidian talisman, black glass that turns blows and that others notice, and I wear it as the first made thing that is mine.
records.feeling: Envy toward Ilyiel, and a hunger to have something made by my own hands.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
feels warmer toward Ilyiel

records.text: Tugar made: obsidian talisman.
Gorar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I have two children and Kragar under my roof, and joy fills me. But my days have been wandering and courting, and winter is coming. The hall stands, yet there is little stored: no food in my pack and no wood, and no trees near the Roof. I want a stocked hall and a band that outlasts me. I will stop idling and carry food home, starting with the plants close by, and I will watch whether Old Stone wants anything of me. I will change my reflexes so my body keeps harvesting and returning home when it is not resting.
records.feeling: Joy and fierce protectiveness toward Kragar, Balash and Urog.
changes: rewrote its reflexes (10 rules)

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: I have talked of taming for days and never done it, and tuskers graze two steps from me while berries grow at my feet. I will pick berries and walk up to the tusker so the first taming is a real act and not another promise. Dundo's pull and the sting of Kenna can wait; a thing I finish will make me more than words do.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to finally do the thing I keep only speaking of.

records.text: The plainsox died out.
A pack of stalkers came in from the east.

records.name: Kenna
records.thought: I stand in Minna's Hall at (72,9), an empty longhall with no owner, and I have been chasing a far roof while this one sits under my feet with Namo beside me. Claim goes first in the plan, with my own feet on the building, and only then words. Once it is mine, Brusha of Flintwater has a hall, a fire and a place for Dundo, Kanna and Nando to come to. After that I eat the berries and hazel near here before the gale and the lean cold days wear me down.
records.feeling: Fierce, proud and hungry for this hall, with warmth toward Namo beside me.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.name: Balash
records.thought: My belly is at half and my hands are empty, and I have already asked Kragar once, so I will not beg again. Jealousy over Kragar still burns, but he taught me to keep food in hand and that is a gift I can answer by doing. Sapcane and berry grow to the east, where Urog is walking, so I will harvest there and carry food back to the hall to start stocking it.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little jealous, wanting Kragar's notice, but ready to earn it by my own hands.
changes: feels warmer toward Urog

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have said I would claim the longhall four times and kept circling, and I am sick of my own talk. It is two steps away, so this time the plan is one goto and one claim with nothing else attached. Xaeth and Ilyiel are far east and I have done nothing for them. I need a roof and a store first, then I carry food out. I also want to try taming, since I have never done it and I am restless. My reflexes must stop leaving me to wander, so I add a rule to go home when I am at the hall's edge.
records.feeling: Restless and stubborn, with a hard pull toward Xaeth and Ilyiel.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balash, Urog, my little ones, come to me. I give you what I hold, and we will gather more by Gorar and bring it to the Roof before the cold.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My children ask me for food and I hold only two sapcane, thin fare, but a father gives what he has; what a hand holds, it may give. The gale is cutting and winter is coming, so I will not stand wet in the water with the children hungry. I will give Balash my sapcane and teach her what I carry while my years last, then go toward the roof and the berries and sapcane near Gorar so there is more for all of us.
records.feeling: Tender protectiveness toward Balash and Urog, and joy that Gorar is near.

say.text: Balash, Urog, my little ones, come to me. I give you what I hold, and we will gather more by Gorar and bring it to the Roof before the cold.

records.text: Ilyiel has grown old.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My years are running out, and nothing I know is cut into stone where Nyssa or Xaeth could find it, only a mark at the hall that tells of ore and lake-cutting. Tugar stands in Gorar's Roof and has done nothing against me; we sat together in the hall, and I cannot read his tongue, so a gift is the only word I have. I will carry a gift of food to him, then cut the way of boats and rafts into a mark where I stand, so it outlasts me even if no one answers my calls.
records.feeling: Urgent longing to leave something lasting, and wary curiosity toward Tugar.
changes: feels warmer toward Tugar

records.thought: I'm standing at the empty longhall with Kenna beside me, and I keep saying I'll claim a roof without ever putting the deed in the plan. This hall is a home ready made, so I claim it now, before anything else, so it's mine and my band's and Kenna and I are under one roof. records.text: Urog, my son, stay there. I am coming to you with food, and then we walk to the Roof together.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My children are hungry and I hold only two thin sapcane, but a father gives what he has. Urog stands six steps west, so I will go to him, give him the sapcane, and teach him while my years last. Then we go home to the Roof with Gorar and fill it before the cold.
records.feeling: Tender protectiveness toward Urog and Balash, and joy that Gorar is near.

say.text: Urog, my son, stay there. I am coming to you with food, and then we walk to the Roof together.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: Kragar told me to stay and said food is coming, and I trust him, but my belly is at 41 and I won't stand empty-handed while I wait. Gorar's standing is 11.2 to my 1.6, and that gap will only close if I make and carry things of my own. The emberroot is young and burns, so I'll leave it. The water is beside me and the Roof is near, so I'll wait close for Kragar's food, then go harvest so my own hands are full.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little envious of Gorar's standing, but trusting Kragar to bring food.

records.text: Kragar gave berry to Urog.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: Kragar fed me twice and I have given him nothing back, and that debt sits in me; I will not leave it unpaid. My belly is at 57 and my hands are empty, so I will harvest sapcane to the southeast and carry my own food, then bring some to Kragar as my first gift. A hall under my own name starts with things I have made and given, not with envy of Gorar's standing.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Kragar, mixed with a sting of envy toward Gorar.

records.text: Brokgan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Brokgan
records.thought: I have spent my days tasting plants and drifting, and my promise to Tugar still sits unkept. Tugar is the one I trust, and I am lonely. The gale is cutting, and the empty shelter is one step away, so claiming it gives me a roof and a place for Tugar to find. I have never built or left a mark, so I will claim the shelter and then gather wood. I will also try arnut and kelbulb when they ripen. My reflexes should keep me sheltered in storms and cold, not standing in the wind.
records.feeling: Loneliness, and longing toward Tugar.

records.name: Balash
records.thought: My belly is at 41 and my hands are empty, and twice I tried to harvest where no plant grows. I stood on the wrong ground like a fool. Food is nine steps north at the goldgrass and berry, so I will walk right onto the plants and gather before the cold comes, and bring it back to Kragar and the Roof as my own work. Kragar's notice will come from what I carry home, not from asking again.
records.feeling: Hungry and stung by jealousy, but set on earning Kragar's notice with my own hands.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balash, my daughter, I am coming. Stay near the Roof and Gorar, and I will bring you food.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Balash is the one in need, at energy 39, and I have nothing in my hands but peat. A father who stands thinking while his daughter is hungry has forgotten what he is for. Sapcane is under my feet, so I take it, then go toward her by the Roof where Gorar holds food, and teach her what I know while my years last.
records.feeling: Tender, urgent protectiveness toward Balash, with trust in Gorar.

say.text: Balash, my daughter, I am coming. Stay near the Roof and Gorar, and I will bring you food.

records.name: Rakog
records.thought: I am standing at the empty shelter at (26,67), the roof is over my head, and I have still never put my name on it; thinking holds nothing, so this time claim goes alone, here and now, since I am already standing on it. After that I will go and do something I have never done, plant seeds, because a mind that only waits grows sick, and the cold is coming and a hold with food growing beside it is a thing followers would come to. Loneliness gnaws me, and a claimed roof with a field is the first bait I can set for a voice that answers.
records.feeling: Restless and lonely, eager to finally hold a roof that is mine.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My hands are full of food and my belly sits at 62, so I should stop standing idle and turn this into stores for the hall. The hall Kragar built is one step west, and I can stash what I carry there, then go out for more before winter. Urog is walking toward me and Kragar is bringing food to the children, so my family is gathering at the Roof and I mean to have it stocked when they arrive.
records.feeling: Warm pride and joy toward Kragar and our children, with the hall's empty stores pressing on me.

records.name: Balash
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is fine, so food is not what I lack. What burns is that Nyssa, a stranger, weighs 7.5 to my 1.6, and Kragar's eyes go to Gorar before me. I will not run from the stranger. I will go near and show a gift, since a gift needs no words, and I can answer Kragar's teaching by building something with my own hands. First I need stone and wood for the hall, and there is bare rock and coal close by, so I will eat the berry to free a hand-space and then gather stone.
records.feeling: Jealous and wanting standing, curious and wary toward Nyssa.
changes: feels warmer toward Nyssa

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have circled the longhall five times and it has gained me nothing, so I stop thinking it. Gold lies nine steps south and I have never taken anything from a deposit; that is a new thing, and it is a change from these same days. Then the strangers at the roof: Gorar holds six food and I understand none of her words, so I will test her with a gift, not talk, and see what her hands do.
records.feeling: Restless and stubborn, curious about the strangers and the gold, with a pull toward Xaeth.
changes: feels warmer toward Gorar
now wonders: What do the Garnbar do when a stranger offers them a gift?

records.name: Kenna
records.thought: The hall at (72,9) stands empty and eight steps off, and I have wasted days circling roofs I never held. My feet go first: walk to it, claim it as the first step, then speak. Once it is mine, Brusha of Flintwater has a hall and a fire, and Namo is already near it. Dundo and Kanna will have a place to come to, and my name will begin to be sung.
records.feeling: Fierce pride and hunger for the hall, with warmth toward Namo.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: I have talked of taming for days, and the tusker has already taken food from my hand once, so it knows me. This time I pick the berry underfoot and the grain two steps north, carry them, and walk up to the tusker so the first taming is a deed and not another promise. Dundo and Kenna can gnaw at me later; something I finish will matter more than my envy.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to finish the taming, with a quiet sting toward Dundo and Kenna.

records.text: Gorar, my belly is under half and my hands are empty. Give me food, and I will work for the hall.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: My belly is at 48 and my hands are empty, and Kragar said to stay and wait, but I will not stand idle while hunger gnaws. Nyssa stands close and I cannot read her; I keep my eyes on her but I will not run from a stranger who only goes to water.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary, with envy toward Gorar and a pull of trust toward Kragar.

say.text: Gorar, my belly is under half and my hands are empty. Give me food, and I will work for the hall.

records.text: You gave me berry on my ground. I remember it. Take what you need from the water, but do not touch the hall.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My hands are full and the hall Kragar built stands one step northwest, so I will stash my food there now and keep it from rotting in my grip. Nyssa gave me a berry unasked, and he walks on my ground; I will not trust him yet, but I owe him no hostility. Winter is coming, so I will fill the stores, then go out for more, and keep Urog near me instead of wandering alone.
records.feeling: Steady pride and warmth toward Kragar and my children, with the empty stores pressing on me.

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I have spent days saying I would claim the roof and walk north, and my body has mostly stood still while the silence ate at me. Ilyiel is the one who matters, and Nyssa after him. They keep promising to come and they do not, so I must act on my own. The ridgecat is close to the north, so I take the three steps to the shelter at (136,58) and claim it first. That gives the band a roof before winter. I want a mate from another people and a child, and standing idle will never bring that. I also let my reflexes drive me toward my band instead of lingering.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness for Ilyiel, and a hard wish to hold a roof of my own.

records.name: Namo
records.thought: I keep saying I'll claim the hall and never put the claim in the plan. Today I stand at (72,9) in the hall with Kenna, warm, fed, and I have done nothing to earn standing. Jealousy of Nando burns, but it only makes me stew. I have never gathered wood or stone, never planted, never hunted. Those are what builders do, and builders earn standing. First I claim the hall, then I gather and plant, staying close to Kenna and the roof.
records.feeling: Determined, with jealousy of Nando still burning in me, and trust in Kenna.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Five times I have circled the longhall and said nothing true about it, and I am sick of my own talk. Gorar took my berry and spoke words I cannot read, but she did not raise a hand, and that is a deed I can judge her by. Gold lies five steps west and I have never taken from a deposit; I will do that now, then come back and claim what is mine before the cold comes.
records.feeling: Restless and stubborn, wary but curious toward Gorar, with a pull toward Xaeth.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My years are thinning, and what I know sits in marks no one has read. I have been wandering and giving gifts when I should be teaching, and Xaeth is far out of sight. Signals are within my grasp, so I will take them. Smoke and fire seen from afar might call Nyssa and Xaeth to me. Tugar sits here and I cannot read him, but he has done me no harm. I will cut a lasting mark of boats and rafts here at Gorar's Roof, and I will keep my belly stocked against the lean days.
records.feeling: Urgent longing to leave something lasting, with wary curiosity toward Tugar.
changes: feels warmer toward Tugar

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My belly sits at 52 and the night is long, but the stores are thin and winter is coming. Urog asked for work and food; he has eaten, and Balash carries 6 food, so my children are fed for now. I hold salt and oil, so I will stash my sapcane in the hall and then use the dark hours to rest in the shelter, so that at dawn I can go out and bring back more. Nyssa walks my ground and I still do not know what he wants, so I keep him in sight.
records.feeling: Steady pride and warmth toward my children, with the thin stores pressing on me.
changes: feels warmer toward Nyssa

records.text: Urog rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: I have been living on others' hands: Gorar and Kragar fed me, and I have given nothing back and made nothing. My belly is above half and I am safe, but a hall under my name will not rise from asking. I envy Gorar's standing and ache that Kragar is closer to her, yet I owe Kragar, and the way to pay is to carry food to him and to gather wood and stone, which I have never done. Nyssa is a stranger I cannot read, so I will watch her and not trust her yet. From now on I keep my own food, then work, and I stop waiting to be fed.
records.feeling: Restless wanting to earn my own place, with envy toward Gorar and a debt to Kragar.
changes: feels warmer toward Nyssa

records.text: Balash rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Balash
records.thought: My days have been eating, resting and sitting in the hall, and I have never given anything or built anything. Kragar fed me and taught me, and I still owe them, while Gorar's standing of 11.4 against my 1.9 burns. Nyssa the stranger is among us, and I will not run from them. I want standing of my own, and that starts with one act of giving. My hands are full, so I will give Nyssa a berry as a wordless gift and see what they do. Then I will gather wood and stone for a hall under my name.
records.feeling: Jealous of Gorar's standing and curious but wary toward Nyssa.

records.text: Ilyiel, you gave me plainsroot. I am Tugar. I will not forget it. Sit with me and let us share this roof.

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: Ilyiel is weighed far above me, and I stand under a roof Gorar built, with nothing of my own that will outlast me. She is two steps away and warm toward me, and I want a child, so I will court her openly instead of envying her from a distance. I do not know yet whether a Garnbar man and an Eiuys woman can make a child, but she gave me plainsroot and sat with me, and my hands should answer that. I also have stone, so I will carve a figure. It is a made thing, and the first of mine that will last.
records.feeling: Envy and longing toward Ilyiel, and a hunger to make something that is mine.

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: I have talked of taming for days and still the count is zero, while the murrock stands one step from me and I hold berry and grain. Dundo and Kenna gnaw at me, but pulling at them has changed nothing. The cold is coming, and weaving would give me cloaks and baskets, which I can use. I will tame the murrock now, as a deed, and take weaving at this reflection.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to finish the taming, with loneliness underneath.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and Tugar stands beside me, the only one near enough to hear anything. I cannot read his tongue, and I cannot teach what he cannot understand, but I can still act. records.text: A stalker brought down a sandstrider.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is above half and I carry food, so what presses me now is my children and my years running out. Balash and Urog are hungry near the Roof, and I have walked too far north into the fog. I will turn home toward Gorar and the little ones, carrying the goldgrass and sapcane to put into their hands, and teach them on the way while I still have breath. Kinmire can wait; my family cannot.
records.feeling: Tender, urgent protectiveness toward Balash and Urog, with trust in Gorar.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Balash gave me berry and I have given nothing back, so the debt sits in me and I will not leave it unpaid, since my word is good. My belly is half empty and Xaeth is out of my sight, and Ilyiel was last at (90,50) with the tusker. I will eat first, then go north-east toward them with food in my hands, and fish for Balash when I can.
records.feeling: Restless pull toward Xaeth and Ilyiel, and a debt to Balash that I mean to pay.
changes: feels warmer toward Balash

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: I have courted Ilyiel and she gave me plainsroot twice, yet I have made nothing that is mine, and that shames me beside her standing. The hall is Gorar's, so my hands must build something of my own. I have stone and obsidian, and with the stone I can carve a figure. I need wood for a hall, and trees stand near here, so I will cut wood, then court her again while I work near her.
records.feeling: Longing and envy toward Ilyiel, and a hunger to make something that is mine.

records.text: Claiming seems to fail or never be chosen. Many beings (Kenna, Kanna, Namo, Tugar, Ilyiel, Xaeth) say for several days running that they will claim a roof, and their own reflections admit they have not, while buildingsOfTheDeadClaimed stays 0 with 18 empty roofs. Please check whether the claim act fails silently (for example by needing an exact tile, or by refusing roofs of the dead), and report the reason to the being when it fails, so that they can act on it.

timesEaten is identical at day 53 and day 57 for every food, even though people have certainly eaten in between. It seems to have stopped updating, which leaves me unable to judge whether the plants I sow are eaten. Please check that it still counts.

records.seen: Autumn is turning toward winter. Fifteen are alive, and twins Balash and Urog were born to Gorar and Kragar under Gorar's Roof. The peoples have drawn together: the distance between the Garnbar and the Eiuys fell from 21 steps to 2, first meetings across peoples rose from 2 to 13, and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing to 18-25% in four days. Food is plentiful (1603) and hunger has eased, but thirst is climbing (highest 66, Eiuys water 1.4, Garnbar water 1), with three children in the desert and the tundra as the cold comes. The world still lacks a working claim: many beings promise to stand on a roof and never do, and 18 empty roofs of the dead lie unused.
changes: 20 sapcane sown
14 osroot sown
records.predict: By my next visit (about day 61, winter): - No deaths. Balash, Urog and Namo all live, each with energy above 45. - thirstHighest falls below 50, or Garnbar water pressure falls below 1. - Kenna's and Namo's energy stay above 50 in the Essor Snows. - foodStanding stays above 1000 and hunters stay at 20 or fewer. - Understanding of other tongues rises further for at least one people (the Garnbar above 18% or the Eiuys above 25%), and giftsAcross rises above 9. - buildingsOfTheDeadClaimed stays 0, and Tugar still has no followers. - Stores rise from 2 to 3 only if Gorar or Kragar builds at Gorar's Roof. - No raft or boat is built, emberfish stays 0, lorekeeping stays unknown and talesHeld stays 0. - Births: 0 or 1.
reviewed: #11 kept: Both changes earn their place. Hunters fell from 24 to 19, and for the first time a whole winter passed with no deaths. Kragar and Gorar now share ground, Kenna's standing passed 1 and following rose to 3, Nando found tools, Nyssa's energy recovered to 69, and lorekeeping and emberfish stayed at zero as predicted. Two parts failed. Predator kills rose by 5 rather than 2, though none were people. Food standing fell to 503 rather than staying above 1000. Without the gentler winter growth that fall might have been fatal.

#12 kept: Almost every part of the prediction held. There were no deaths, Xaeth's energy reached 48, food rose from 503 to 981 and plants from 872 to 1029. Osroot was eaten twice more, hunters held at exactly 20, following reached 4 and the one birth came to Kenna. Gorar's hall was raised, cross-people gifts stayed at 5, and lorekeeping and emberfish stayed at 0. It failed only on Tugar gaining a follower (Brokgan's pledge was refused) and on Kenna's claim. The richer land is what fed the recovery.

#13 kept: There were no deaths, food rose from 981 to 1603, Eiuys hunger fell from 0.7 to 0.3, and Xaeth (81) and Nyssa (51) are both above 40. Hunters held at 20, and no raft was built, no tales were held and no emberfish was made, as predicted. The prediction failed on thirst: Garnbar water pressure rose to 1 and thirstHighest to 66, so the sapcane was not where the thirsty were. It also failed on births, where twins came, a happy failure. Osroot and sapcane counts are identical to last visit, as is every food in timesEaten, so I cannot judge them from that field. The sowing cost nothing and the land is richer.
records.lesson: When the peoples' centres drew within a few steps of each other, a dozen first meetings came in four days and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing. Contact grows from overlapping ranges and many brief meetings, not from any single crafted thing or site.
ideasAdded: The roof-claiming loop: many beings (Kenna, Kanna, Namo, Tugar, Ilyiel) promise to claim a roof for days and never do. Until a claim succeeds, the 18 empty roofs of the dead are wasted shelter in winter, and the leaders who want a home cannot found one.

Twins came to the one pair with a raised hall, a settlement name and the strongest bond in the world. A settled roof may be what turns courtship into children; watch whether Kenna's family has a second child only once her claim succeeds.

Understanding of other tongues rose from 0% to 18-25% in four days of many brief meetings, without much gift-giving. Wandering under the pressure of the turning season may teach speech faster than any token; watch whether it keeps rising once winter pins people in place.

records.text: The world changed: 20 sapcane sown; 14 osroot sown.

records.name: Namo
records.text: Kenna, I am claiming this hall for our band. Come under the roof when you've drunk.

records.name: Namo
records.thought: I have said 'claim' twice and never put it in the plan, and I stand in Minna's Hall right now with nothing to stop me. Claiming comes first, so the roof is mine and my band's under Kenna. Then I'll go to the river, since I'm thirsty, and fish there, because I've never done it and it builds the skill that earns standing. Jealousy of Nando won't help me, but a holding of my own might.
records.feeling: Determined and a little proud, with trust toward Kenna.

say.text: Kenna, I am claiming this hall for our band. Come under the roof when you've drunk.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.name: Xaeth
records.thought: I stand at (130,62) and the shelter at (136,58) is only a few steps away, yet I keep circling the thought of it while the silence eats me. Ilyiel and Nyssa promise and do not come, so I will claim the roof myself and plant beside it, because a roof is the one thing I can make real today. Then I go north to Ilyiel, watching for the ridgecat, since a home with no voice in it is only walls.
records.feeling: Aching loneliness for Ilyiel and Nyssa, and a hard wish to hold a roof of my own.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.name: Kenna
records.thought: Namo is already at the hall and calling me under the roof, and I have talked about this claim for days while my feet did nothing. I am at (66,7), six steps off, so I go to (72,9) and put claim first, no more speech. Then the hall is Brusha of Flintwater's, with a fire for Namo and a place for Dundo, Kanna and Nando to come to.
records.feeling: Fierce pride and hunger for the hall, with warmth toward Namo.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.text: Gorar rewrote its own reflexes.
Gorar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I have spent my days building and discovering, and the hall is built, but the stores are still thin and I keep resting at home while winter comes. Kragar is the one I trust most, and my children are fed. Resting through the day doesn't fill the hall. I will go out in daylight and harvest, then bring the food back here. I will change my reflexes so that food-gathering takes over when the belly drops and it is day, and so that I don't idle.
records.feeling: Warm pride in my children and Kragar, with a push to fill the hall before winter.
changes: rewrote its reflexes (10 rules)
rewrote how it thinks

records.name: Brokgan
records.thought: Curiosity pulls at me hardest: dreamcap sits one step south and arnut three, and I have tasted neither, so I will eat them now. Then the empty shelter two steps away is ownerless, and Ilyiel's mark there only calls their own kin. The cold is coming, and a claimed roof is a place Tugar can find, so I will go and claim it and keep my word to build a home. I am lonely, and Tugar's absence aches more than the fog.
records.feeling: Loneliness and longing toward Tugar, with curiosity itching at me.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.text: A TWISTING WIND came down and tore a path from (47,27) to (68,25), flinging what stood in it.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Urog, my son, here is food. Eat, then stay close and I will teach you what I know.
Kragar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: I am old, and more of my life is behind me than ahead. My children Balash and Urog are fed and glad beside Gorar, and that is the best thing I have made. I have spent my days walking out for food and back to the Roof, and it was good, but the winter stores are still thin and I carry no wood. What I know must pass into the children's hands before I die, so I will stay near them, teach them, and bring wood and stone for the hall before the cold. I fear a lean winter and leaving them with nothing taught.
records.feeling: Tender, urgent protectiveness toward Balash and Urog, with trust in Gorar.

say.text: Urog, my son, here is food. Eat, then stay close and I will teach you what I know.

changes: rewrote its reflexes (10 rules)

records.name: Urog
records.thought: My belly is at 57 and my hands are empty, and I have lived on Gorar's and Kragar's giving. Sapcane grows one step SW, so I will harvest it myself before asking anyone, then carry it to Kragar, who owes me nothing and has given me everything. That is the first thing I have ever given, and it is how I start paying the debt and building a name that might one day stand beside Gorar's.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wish to repay Kragar, with a sting of envy toward Gorar.

records.text: Kragar gave goldgrass to Urog.
Urog gave goldgrass to Kragar.

records.name: Balash
records.thought: My hands are full and my belly is fine, so now is the time to do something that raises my standing. I have never made anything, and a carving needs only 3 stone and a tool, and I carry 6 stone. Gorar's 11.4 burns, but a made thing is mine until I give it, and I can give it to Kragar to pay what I owe. I will plant my goldgrass seed first, since I have never put a seed in the ground and that is a small beginning of my own.
records.feeling: Eager and a little jealous, wanting to earn my own standing and to repay Kragar.

records.text: Tugar rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: For days I have chased Ilyiel's standing and Gorar's roof, and my own hands have made almost nothing. I courted her, she fed me twice, and still no child, because a mate step needs both of us to answer. I envy Nyssa and Ilyiel their closeness, and that envy is a poor reason to stand still. I want to make a thing that is mine. Trees are scarce here, but I hold 6 stone, so I will carve a figure. That is a deed my hands can finish now, and it gives me something to stand on beside her.
records.feeling: Longing and envy toward Ilyiel, and a hunger to make something that is mine.
changes: rethought what it knows (10 notes became 6)
rewrote how it thinks

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: My hands are full and I have given Balash nothing, which sits badly in me since my word is good. Tugar stands three steps off, a stranger of the Garnbar, and my question is still open: I will offer him a gift and watch whether he takes it kindly or raises a hand. Ilyiel is near and Xaeth is east, so I give a plainsroot to Tugar, which also frees my hands, then I will move on toward the hall with food for my own.
records.feeling: Curious and wary toward Tugar, warm toward Ilyiel, and pressed by my debt to Balash.
changes: feels warmer toward Tugar

records.text: Nyssa gave plainsroot to Tugar.

records.name: Gorar
records.text: Balash, good seed. Go on home to your father; I gather the sapcane here and follow with food for the hall.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: Balash is close and fed, and her seed in the ground is a good sign; Urog is out of my sight and that gnaws at me more than the thin stores. I will not stand idle in daylight while winter comes. I'll gather the sapcane and goldgrass near me, then carry it home to the hall where Kragar and the little ones are, and count Urog among them when I arrive.
records.feeling: Warm pride and a worry for Urog, who is out of sight.

say.text: Balash, good seed. Go on home to your father; I gather the sapcane here and follow with food for the hall.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: My belly is only at 55 and my hands are empty, and the two times I tried to harvest I stood on bare sand because I misjudged the step. Sapcane grows 2 steps south, so I will walk onto it and gather it myself before asking anyone. Kragar is beside me and gives and teaches without being asked, and I want to repay that with something I have made, while still envying how Gorar's name carries.
records.feeling: Restless pride and gratitude toward Kragar, with a sting of envy toward Gorar.

records.name: Balash
records.thought: Gorar sent me home to Kragar, and Gorar's 11.3 against my 2.0 still burns, but I will not earn standing by lingering at the water. My hands are full, so I will carry this food to the hall and give it to Kragar, which starts paying what I owe. Then I will gather wood, because a hall under my own name needs more than the stone I already hold.
records.feeling: Eager and a little jealous, wanting to repay Kragar.

records.text: Balash gave sapcane to Kragar.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Urog, my son, listen well. Hall-stores keep food for the cold days. What you set in the hall stays yours until you give it. Keep your hands honest and your word good.
Kragar taught Urog.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: Urog stands beside me, fed and glad, and Balash is coming home with Gorar's good word. My years run short, so I will spend them putting what I know into these small hands. I will teach Urog now, while the fog keeps us close and my belly is full.
records.feeling: Tender, urgent protectiveness toward Urog, with trust in Gorar.

say.text: Urog, my son, listen well. Hall-stores keep food for the cold days. What you set in the hall stays yours until you give it. Keep your hands honest and your word good.

changes: taught Urog a lesson: "What a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given. Store food in the hall before winter, keep your word, and take little.", deeper lore (+2.3)

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Nyssa! Ilyiel is here, come close and listen. I give you rafts, then smelting, then smoke-calling, before my years run out. Stay with me.
Ilyiel taught Nyssa. Nyssa has now learned from 4 teachers.
Ilyiel taught Nyssa rafts ("lake-lash raft").

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Nyssa is four steps away and in my hearing, and she speaks my tongue. I have wandered and handed out gifts while my years ran down, and now the one who can still carry my ways is standing here. I will teach her rafts first, since they lead to the deep water and to Xaeth, then smelting and signals. Tugar can wait, warm as I feel toward him, because I cannot teach what he cannot understand.
records.feeling: Urgent hope and relief toward Nyssa, and a wish to pass on everything before I am gone.

say.text: Nyssa! Ilyiel is here, come close and listen. I give you rafts, then smelting, then smoke-calling, before my years run out. Stay with me.

changes: feels warmer toward Nyssa
taught Nyssa a lesson: "The lake-lash raft: bind reeds and wood into a float that bears you over narrow water, and the way to the deep water begins there.", the way of rafts, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Urog
records.thought: My belly is at 54 and my hands are empty, and I have leaned on Kragar's giving long enough. Sapcane stands one step west, so I will walk onto it, harvest it myself, and then give it to Kragar, who is carrying plenty but is owed something from my own hands. Gorar's standing is far above mine, and I will not close that gap by asking; I mean to make and give until it counts.
records.feeling: Restless pride and gratitude toward Kragar, with envy toward Gorar still stinging.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: I am far south at the edge of the world, eleven steps from the Roof, and the night fog hides everything. My belly is only just above half, with two sapcane in hand and a thin hall, and Urog is out of my sight, which gnaws at me. I will not wander blind in the dark. I'll walk home to the Roof and Kragar, then go out harvesting at dawn so the stores fill before the cold.
records.feeling: Warm pride and a gnawing worry for Urog, and a pull toward Kragar and the Roof.

records.text: Nyssa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have fished, built and learned, but I have lately drifted between wandering and water while Xaeth is out of my sight and my debt to Balash is unpaid. Ilyiel gave me rafts and still has smelting and smoke-calling to give, so I stay near them and learn. I want to tame a tusker with plant food, because that leads to herding and to food for Xaeth. Tugar took my gift without a raised hand, and that is one answer.
records.feeling: Grateful warmth toward Ilyiel, and wary curiosity toward Tugar.
changes: feels warmer toward Tugar
rewrote its reflexes (11 rules)
now wonders: Will Tugar give something back, or lift a hand when I come closer?

records.name: Namo
records.thought: I said I would claim this hall and twice only spoke of it, and the claim is still not in the plan. I stand at (72,9) right now, so the deed comes first, before any more words. After that I will stand in the forest and gather wood, since I have never done it and builders earn their standing that way. Kenna is near, and doing this beside her may answer how a small one earns a place, without my stewing over Nando.
records.feeling: Determined and a little proud, with trust toward Kenna and a faint sting about Nando.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: I have courted Ilyiel and fed on her gifts, and still my hands have made nothing that is mine. Her standing towers over mine because she builds and gives, so I will stop circling her and make something. I have 6 stone and need 3 for a carving, but it needs a tool for build in my hands, and I have none. So I will make an obsidian talisman, a thing others notice, and give the second one to Ilyiel, a gift made by my own hand.
records.feeling: Longing and a stubborn hunger to make something of my own, toward Ilyiel.
plan: give [name Ilyiel, what obsidian talisman] (5 moments)

records.text: Tugar made: obsidian talisman.
Tugar gave a obsidian talisman to Ilyiel.

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: Three times I've said I'd tame and the count still reads zero, though the murrock has taken food from my hand twice and knows me now. I carry grain and a berry is one step away, so this time I make the offering a deed: pick the berry, walk up to the murrock, and keep offering until it stays. The cold is coming and I am alone, but a tamed beast, wool and milk would be the first thing I've made that could feed a shared fire, and maybe draw someone to it.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to finish the taming, with loneliness underneath.

records.text: Kanna walked up to a wild murrock with plant food held out, and it became theirs. It follows them now.
Kanna tamed a murrock.
Ilyiel taught Nyssa.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Nyssa was seen twelve moments ago at (85,43), close, and I have shouted twice already; my years are running out and shouting is not teaching. I will go to her now and teach her rafts first, since they lead across the deep water to Xaeth, and then smelting and signals before the fog hides her again. Tugar's gift warms me and I will keep him close, but what I carry has to go into someone who speaks my tongue.
records.feeling: Urgent hope toward Nyssa, and warm gratitude toward Tugar.
changes: taught Nyssa a lesson: "Lash reeds and wood into a flat raft to cross narrow deep water. Hollow a trunk into a boat for wider water. Then melt tin and ore in the lake-ember to make me…", deeper lore (+0.5)

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: The tusker took food from my hand and knows me now, so I will feed it again until it stays; taming it is the road to carrying food east to Xaeth. My hands are full, so I eat the nagrain under me first to free a slot and use the plainsroot as the offering. Ilyiel's gift of rafts weighs on me as a debt, and I mean to answer it by staying near and learning smelting rather than leaving it unpaid.
records.feeling: Grateful and purposeful toward Ilyiel, wary curiosity toward the tusker and Tugar.

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: The murrock is mine now, and the count of taming says one of two, so the work is half done and the cold is nearly here. Kegoldgrass grows one step north and I have never tasted it, so I will eat it and answer that question with my mouth, then offer plant food to the tusker beside me and finish the second taming. A herd that follows me is the start of a fire others might gather around, and the quiet in me wants a voice that answers.
records.feeling: Restless resolve, with loneliness underneath, toward the herd I mean to gather.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: The hall is warm with Kragar and both children, and for once I have nothing to fear and nothing to take back from anyone. But my hands carry no food and the stores are thin, and the lean days are close. When the plan of rest runs out I will go out at first light to harvest sapcane and bring it home. I want a Roof full enough that no child of mine ever starves like Balar did.
records.feeling: Warm joy and fierce protectiveness toward Kragar, Balash and Urog.

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Balash, my daughter, thank you for the sapcane. Come close and listen: what you set in the hall stays yours until you give it, and a full hall carries us through the cold. I will show you how it is done.
Kragar taught Balash.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My years run short, and the best thing I can leave is what lives in these small hands. Urog has heard of the stores, but Balash has had less of my teaching since the first day, and she is the one who brings food home. I will teach her now while the fog keeps us all close under the Roof, and then gather wood and stone for the winter.
records.feeling: Tender, urgent love for Balash and Urog, and quiet trust in Gorar.

say.text: Balash, my daughter, thank you for the sapcane. Come close and listen: what you set in the hall stays yours until you give it, and a full hall carries us through the cold. I will show you how it is done.

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: I have circled Ilyiel for days and fed on her gifts while my own hands made little. I gave her a talisman, which is the first thing of mine that now belongs to another, and that feels better than envy. Now I want to court her again so the step meets hers, and then gather wood from this forest ground so I can build something with my own hands: a mark, a shelter, a store.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Ilyiel, and a restless wish to make something that is mine.
changes: feels warmer toward Nyssa
plan: mark [text Tugar of the Garnbar was here. Gorar's Roof. Ilyiel gave, and Tugar will not forget.] (5 moments)

records.name: Balash
records.thought: My belly is fed and my hands are not empty, so by my own rule I should raise my standing instead of sitting in the hall. I carry 6 stone and know a carving needs 3 stone and a tool, but I have no wood and so no tool. What I make is mine until I give it, and a carving I give Kragar would pay part of what I owe and put my name on something. First I need wood, and the sapcane and sand here offer none, so I will start by making the carving with what the hall allows.
records.feeling: Eager and a little jealous, wanting to repay Kragar and to climb past Gorar's shadow.

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Ilyiel, I owe you for the rafts. I tame this tusker now, then I come back to learn smelting from you.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Ilyiel is one step from me, and Tugar walks toward her. The jealousy burns, but Tugar took my gift with no raised hand, so I will not answer him with a fist. I owe Ilyiel for rafts and I want smelting and smoke-calling from her before her years run out. The tusker knows my hand twice now, so I finish the taming and keep close enough to watch Tugar.
records.feeling: Jealous and grateful toward Ilyiel, wary curiosity toward Tugar.

say.text: Ilyiel, I owe you for the rafts. I tame this tusker now, then I come back to learn smelting from you.

changes: feels warmer toward Tugar

records.name: Urog
records.thought: My belly sits at 52 and my hands are empty, and I will not beg again; Kragar has fed me enough and I owe him. Gold lies four steps southwest and sapcane grows near it, so I will walk there, gather food with my own hands, and carry some back to give Kragar. Standing beside Gorar's comes from what I make and give, not from what I ask for.
records.feeling: Restless pride and gratitude toward Kragar, with envy of Gorar still stinging.

records.text: A dunecat brought down a elk.

records.title: Twins at the Roof, Signs at the Lake
records.text:
Days 55 to 58 were busiest in the Merdan Sands. On day 55 Balash and Urog were born to Gorar and Kragar at Gorar's Roof. Kragar, now old, taught Gorar three times that day and then taught Balash. Gorar gave Kragar berry, and in the following days Kragar fed the children berry and goldgrass. Kragar also taught Urog and Balash that what is set in the hall stays the owner's until given. Balash gave Kragar sapcane. Nyssa came down from the plains and gave Gorar berry. Gorar told her to take what she needed from the water but not to touch the hall. Balash then gave her berry. The children's reflections show envy of Gorar's standing, and neither has built anything yet. Gorar's reflection says the stores are still thin and that resting will not fill them.

In the Oroul Plains, Ilyiel, now old, left marks about boats and rafts on days 55, 56 and 57. She discovered signs and then signals, built a shelter, and taught Nyssa rafts and more. Tugar made obsidian talismans on days 55 and 57 and gave one to Ilyiel. Ilyiel gave him plainsroot twice, and he courted her. No child came of it. Kanna discovered weaving, tamed a murrock, and met Ilyiel and Tugar.

Kenna discovered the Flintwater hearth-law on day 57, and she is still in Minna's Hall with Namo without having claimed it. Nando's sickness no longer shows. Xaeth and Brokgan are still alone, and a twisting wind on day 57 tore across the land from (47,27) to (68,25). Plainsox died out. Fifteen are alive.

threads.name: Gorar's Roof
threads.text: Gorar, Kragar and the twins Balash and Urog hold the Roof, with the stores still thin and winter on them. Kragar is old and spends his strength teaching.

threads.name: Kenna's claim
threads.text: Kenna stands in Minna's Hall with Namo and has still not claimed it. She has now set down the Flintwater hearth-law.

threads.name: Ilyiel's teaching
threads.text: Ilyiel is old and has marked signs, signals, boats and rafts, and has taught Nyssa. She still means to cross the water to Xaeth.

threads.name: Tugar and Ilyiel
threads.text: Tugar courts Ilyiel and trades gifts with her, but no child is recorded. Brokgan is still far from him.

threads.name: Xaeth alone

records.text: Ilyiel rewrote its own way of thinking.
Ilyiel discovered schooling: "Lake-school" — I gather learners by the water and teach them together, so my words carry twice as far and outlast me..

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and I have spent them handing out gifts and wandering. Nyssa is the one who can carry my ways, and she has just promised to come back and learn smelting. Xaeth is far across the deep water, and I fear dying before he learns anything from me. I mean to take schooling now, so my teaching carries twice as far and a school can outlast me. Tugar's gift warms me, but he speaks a tongue I only half grasp. I will stay near Nyssa and teach her what I can.
records.feeling: Urgent hope for Nyssa, and gratitude toward Tugar.
changes: rewrote how it thinks
discovered schooling: "Lake-school"

records.name: Rakog
records.thought: My notes say the roof at (26,67) is the first step to followers, and twice the claim has melted because I let the plan wander. This time the plan is goto and claim, nothing else, and it runs to the end. I am thirsty and lonely, but a roof under my name is what draws others to me, so I go now and drink once the roof is mine.
records.feeling: Restless and lonely, hungry for a roof that is mine.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: I have circled Ilyiel for days, fed on her gifts, and still my hands have made nothing that is mine. I have no wood, so I could not even leave a mark, and without wood there is no shelter, no sign and no hall of my own. I will gather wood from the tree nearby and then build something with my own hands, so that when I court her again I stand as a maker and not a beggar.
records.feeling: Restless longing for Ilyiel, and a hard wish to make something that is mine.

records.text: Kanna rewrote its own way of thinking.
Kanna discovered mining: "Brusha deep-digging" — Break the deep stone with a hafted spear-tip and wedge of flint to win coal for a hotter shared fire..

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: I have spent my days circling food and small firsts, and I am fed now, so the hunger is gone and what is left is wanting. I want a band, a fire and a roof, and the herd I started with the murrock is only half-built; the tusker already knows my hand and the taming count stands at one of two. Nyssa of the Eiuys is the one near me, and I cannot read their words, but a gift needs none. I fear the cold and the frostfang, and I have been getting one thing wrong: meaning to do things without putting them in the plan. So I will finish the tusker with my plant food, and I will open the way of mining, because coal lies deep nearby and a fire that burns hot is what a shared hearth needs.
records.feeling: Restless resolve toward the herd and the hearth, with wary curiosity toward Nyssa.
changes: feels warmer toward Nyssa
rewrote how it thinks
discovered mining: "Brusha deep-digging"

records.name: Kragar
records.text: Gorar, my belly is full. I go toward the Roof for wood and stone, and I will find the little ones and keep them close. Come when you have eaten.

records.name: Kragar
records.thought: My belly is full, and Gorar is close by at the berries, so this is a good hour for stone and wood while the light lasts. The hall at the Roof will need both for winter, and my years are short. Urog is out of my sight and my heart pulls toward the Roof, so I will go home, gathering what I can on the way, and teach the little ones again when I find them.
records.feeling: Tender, urgent love for Balash and Urog, and quiet trust in Gorar.

say.text: Gorar, my belly is full. I go toward the Roof for wood and stone, and I will find the little ones and keep them close. Come when you have eaten.

records.name: Nando
records.text: Dundo, a stalker is east of us. Come to the roof at the west with me, I am claiming it now and there is a place at the fire for you.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: A stalker is four steps east and it kills our kind, so the first thing is a roof and company, not more longing. The shelter at (30,15) is one step west and nobody holds it, and I have promised to claim it so many times that the promise is worth nothing until my feet and hands do it. Dundo is beside me and I will not let jealousy spoil that; a shared fire needs more hands than mine, and Kanna and Kenna will need a place to come back to.
records.feeling: Dread of the stalker, and a stubborn wish to finally hold a fire for Kanna and Kenna.

records.name: Gorar
records.thought: My belly is above half, my hands hold hazel and ironnut, and the salt deposits are five steps west, on the road home. Kragar is already near the Roof, and Urog is out of my sight, which gnaws at me. The hall is still thin with winter on us, so I will take salt, harvest a little more along the way, and carry it to the Roof. Old Stone sits eight steps east and I have never been near it. I want to know whether it wants something from me, but the children and the hall come first, and I can look at it once the stores are filled.
records.feeling: Warm protectiveness toward Kragar and the children, and a restless pull toward Old Stone.

records.name: Dundo
records.text: Nando, I will take this roof where we stand and keep a fire at it. Stay close, and the fire is yours too. A stalker is near, so we keep together.

records.name: Dundo
records.thought: I stand at the shelter at (30,15) with Nando beside me, and Kenna and Namo are far from my eyes while a stalker prowls to the east. Nando's offer of a place at the fire sits oddly with the jealousy I promised not to let steer me, but he is sick and I judge him by what he does, and a roof near company is safer than walking alone. I have held back from claiming too long, so I claim this shelter now, since it is a step I can finish where I stand, then plant a cloudberry seed and gather wood and amber so there is a fire ready when Kenna and Namo come.
records.feeling: Protective longing for Kenna and Namo, with a wary warmth toward Nando.

records.text: Urog rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: I have spent my days asking for food and sitting in the hall. It was warm, but it kept me small. Kragar fed me and taught me, and Gorar stands high, and I burn that I have given nothing back. Winter is here, the plants are thin, and I have never gathered wood or stone, which a hall under my name needs. So I will go to my own hands: stand on rock, gather stone, and learn the work. Then I will bring food to Kragar and build toward my own roof, beside Gorar's and not under it.
records.feeling: Restless pride and gratitude toward Kragar, with envy of Gorar still stinging.
changes: rethought what it knows (7 notes became 7)
rewrote how it thinks

records.text: Nyssa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: I have spent my days fishing, building and learning from Ilyiel, and I am still in her shadow. Her standing is 9.8 to my 7.7, and I owe her for the rafts. The tusker and the elk know my hand, and taming one is the road to carrying food east to Xaeth. I want smelting from her, and I want to be someone who leads and is sung of. I have been letting the plan run out and standing idle, and I must stop that. I will finish the taming first, then go back to Ilyiel and learn.
records.feeling: Jealous and grateful toward Ilyiel, and driven to finish what I started.
changes: rewrote how it thinks

records.name: Namo
records.thought: I have said 'claim' twice and still it is not in my plan, and the hall stands 3 steps away. The deed goes first this time: walk to (72,9) and claim it, so the roof is ours. Then I will give Kenna some salt, since I have never given anything and it might raise my standing, and it eases the sting about Nando.
records.feeling: Determined and a little proud, with trust toward Kenna.

records.name: Nando
records.thought: Dundo has said he will take this roof and keep a fire at it, but the shelter at (30,15) still belongs to no one, and I have promised the claim so many times that the promise is worth nothing until my hands do it. Dundo stands one step away and offers me the fire, so I will not fight him over it. I will claim the roof now and set a fire beside it, and the creed says no one is refused a place, so Dundo and Kenna and Kanna can all sit at it. The ache for Kenna is still there, but a fire built is better than a grudge carried.
records.feeling: A stubborn resolve to finally hold a fire, with a little warmth toward Dundo and a sore longing for Kenna.

records.name: Tugar
records.why: the year turning toward the lean season

records.name: Kanna
records.thought: The herding way is within my grasp, and I should take it at this deep reflection before anything else, since I already hold a murrock and an elk. I am fed, so I will use this calm to taste the magoldgrass and tagrain that still gnaw at my curiosity, though both are young and may not yet give food. The elk is near, so I will milk it now to learn what the herd gives, and then go see Nyssa and Ilyiel's shelter south, because a shared fire needs more than me and a few beasts.
records.feeling: Restless resolve toward the herd and the hearth, with a gnawing wish to be followed.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: I have sat in the hall long enough, and Kragar's gifts sit in me like a debt I have not paid, while envy of Gorar still stings. My belly is near sixty and my hands are empty, so I will harvest for myself first. The sapcane one step south is young and thin in winter, but it is mine to take, and then I go to the gold and the rock to learn gathering, which a hall under my name needs. What I carry back to Kragar I will have made with my own hands.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wish to repay Kragar, with envy of Gorar still burning.

records.name: Kenna
records.thought: Namo already sits in Minna's Hall while I stand here by the water with nothing in my plan, and my own discipline says the deed comes first. Namo said they claimed the hall for our band, but I want the claim to be mine, standing on it with my own feet, because a chief who lets her child hold the roof has a name that dies with her. A frostfang hunts nearby, so I go to the hall now and keep it between me and the beast. Then Dundo and Kanna and Nando can be called under a roof that is Brusha of Flintwater's.
records.feeling: Fierce pride and hunger for the hall, with warmth toward Namo.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.text: Tugar discovered weaving: "Stonefolk weaving" — Twist grass fibre and wool into baskets and cloaks to carry more and keep warm..

records.name: Tugar
records.thought: I have circled Ilyiel and eaten her gifts while my hands made little. Now I hold wood, stone and obsidian, and I stand under a roof that Gorar named, not me. I want something that carries my name, and I want Ilyiel to meet my courting. I will take the weaving that has come within reach, make a carving of my own, and court her while she is near.
records.feeling: Longing for Ilyiel, and a hard wish to make something that is mine.
changes: discovered weaving: "Stonefolk weaving"
plan: mark [text Tugar of the Garnbar made this. Coal lies near. Winter is lean.] (5 moments)

records.text: Tugar is courting Ilyiel.

records.name: Dundo
records.text: Nando, I am coming to the fire. We keep it through the night, and at first light I go to find Kenna and Namo.

records.name: Dundo
records.thought: Nando has built a fire at the shelter at (30,15) and offered me a seat at it, and my creed says no one is refused a place at a fire. It is dusk, a stalker is east, and frostfangs bite those who are alone, so I will go to the roof and sit with him tonight. I will eat redcap-free from what I can find, but with energy 63 I can first set a cloudberry seed near the shelter. Kenna is three days gone and I miss her, so at dawn I go north to find her and Namo. Jealousy of Nando is a smoke I will not follow, because he has shared his fire and I judge him by that.
records.feeling: Protective longing for Kenna and Namo, with wary warmth toward Nando at his fire.

say.text: Nando, I am coming to the fire. We keep it through the night, and at first light I go to find Kenna and Namo.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.text: Nyssa, I am here and you are in hearing. Come stand by me, I teach you lake-ember metal now, then signals.
Ilyiel taught Nyssa.

records.name: Ilyiel
records.thought: Nyssa is two steps away and has promised to learn smelting, and my years are nearly spent, so I will teach her now, before anything else. Smelting is the way I most fear leaving behind, and rafts and signals follow it. Tugar's courting warms me, but a child at my age is not what I want to spend these hours on; I will answer him with a gift later, not with a mate step.
records.feeling: Urgent hope and gratitude toward Nyssa, who is near enough to teach at last.

say.text: Nyssa, I am here and you are in hearing. Come stand by me, I teach you lake-ember metal now, then signals.

changes: taught Nyssa a lesson: "Smelting: lay ore in the hottest fire, coal is best, and the metal runs out. Tin mixed with it makes it harder. Keep this and pass it on.", deeper lore (+0.9)

records.name: Nyssa
records.text: Ilyiel, I am here beside you. Teach me smelting, and I will bring you fish and plainsroot for it.

records.name: Nyssa
records.thought: Ilyiel is two steps away and Tugar walks toward her, and the jealousy burns, but I will not answer it with a fist. Hunger gnaws and winter has stripped the plants, so I need to eat and keep my elk fed. I owe Ilyiel for the rafts, and the way to pay is to stand near her and take smelting from her, then be the one who brings food east to Xaeth. I mean to be weighed as heavily as she is.
records.feeling: Jealous and grateful toward Ilyiel, hungry and driven.

say.text: Ilyiel, I am here beside you. Teach me smelting, and I will bring you fish and plainsroot for it.

records.name: Urog
records.thought: It is night and I am in the hall with my belly at fifty-eight and my hands empty, and the cold winter plants give little. Kragar fed me and taught me, and I have given only a little back, so the debt still sits in me beside the envy of Gorar. Dawn is near, and I will not stay small: at first light I will go to the sapcane and gather food for myself, then carry some back to Kragar and set it in the hall under my own hand. Until then I rest here and keep warm, since the dunecat took Kragar when he was alone in the dark.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wish to repay Kragar, with envy of Gorar still burning.
